issues.description: Tests share mutable state through the global 'todos' array, causing test interdependence and unpredictable failures
issues.suggestion: Add beforeEach/afterEach hooks to reset the todos array state before each test: beforeEach(() => { todos.length = 0; }) or mock the module to isolate test state

issues.description: Test assertion is too weak - only checks that array length is greater than 0, not that the specific todo was added
issues.suggestion: Assert the exact expected state: expect(todos).toContainEqual({ text: 'Buy milk', completed: false }) or expect(todos[todos.length - 1]).toBe('Buy milk')

issues.description: Test depends on side effects from previous tests or assumes todos array state, making it fragile and order-dependent
issues.suggestion: Ensure test isolation by resetting state in beforeEach and explicitly setting up required state: const initialLength = todos.length; addTodo('Test item'); expect(todos.length).toBe(initialLength + 1); removeTodo(0); expect(todos.length).toBe(initialLength)

issues.description: removeTodo test doesn't verify which item was removed or that the correct item was removed, only that count decreased
issues.suggestion: Add assertions to verify the correct item was removed: const item = 'Temp item'; addTodo(item); removeTodo(todos.findIndex(t => t === item)); expect(todos).not.toContain(item)

issues.description: Missing test suite organization with describe() block, making test output less readable and harder to group related tests
issues.suggestion: Wrap tests in a describe block: describe('Todo Functions', () => { /* tests here */ })

issues.description: No tests for edge cases like removing invalid indices, adding empty todos, or boundary conditions
issues.suggestion: Add edge case tests: test('removeTodo handles invalid index gracefully', () => { expect(() => removeTodo(-1)).not.toThrow(); })

issues.description: Entire test file is on single lines without proper formatting, significantly reducing readability
issues.suggestion: Format code with proper line breaks and indentation using prettier or similar formatter

issues.description: Direct mutation of imported 'todos' array indicates poor encapsulation in the module under test
issues.suggestion: Consider refactoring todo.js to provide a getTodos() function instead of exporting mutable state, enabling better test isolation

codeQuality.summary: This test file has critical flaws in test isolation due to shared mutable state between tests, making them order-dependent and prone to false positives/negatives. The assertions are too weak and don't verify actual behavior beyond array length changes. While basic test structure exists, the lack of proper setup/teardown hooks and edge case coverage significantly undermines test reliability and maintainability.

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test validates that addTodo actually stores the correct todo text/content
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('addTodo stores the correct todo text', () => { const initialLength = todos.length; addTodo('Buy milk'); expect(todos[todos.length - 1]).toBe('Buy milk'); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test covers adding an empty string, which could be invalid input
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('addTodo with empty string should throw error or ignore', () => { expect(() => addTodo('')).toThrow(); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test covers null or undefined input to addTodo
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('addTodo with null throws error', () => { expect(() => addTodo(null)).toThrow(); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test validates removeTodo with invalid index (negative, out of bounds, non-integer)
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('removeTodo with negative index should throw error', () => { expect(() => removeTodo(-1)).toThrow(); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test validates removeTodo with out-of-bounds index
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('removeTodo with index >= todos.length should throw error', () => { const outOfBounds = todos.length + 5; expect(() => removeTodo(outOfBounds)).toThrow(); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test confirms that removeTodo removes the correct item (by index)
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('removeTodo removes the correct item', () => { addTodo('First'); addTodo('Second'); addTodo('Third'); removeTodo(1); expect(todos).not.toContain('Second'); expect(todos).toContain('First'); expect(todos).toContain('Third'); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test validates removeTodo when todos array is empty
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('removeTodo on empty array should throw error', () => { todos.length = 0; expect(() => removeTodo(0)).toThrow(); })

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test validates the initial state of the todos array
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('todos array should be initially empty or defined', () => { expect(Array.isArray(todos)).toBe(true); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test validates behavior with duplicate todos
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('addTodo allows duplicate items', () => { addTodo('Buy milk'); addTodo('Buy milk'); const duplicates = todos.filter(t => t === 'Buy milk'); expect(duplicates.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: No test covers very long strings or special characters
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('addTodo handles special characters', () => { const specialTodo = 'Buy <script>alert(1)</script> & "milk"'; addTodo(specialTodo); expect(todos).toContain(specialTodo); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: Tests share the same todos array state, causing test interdependence and potential flakiness
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Add beforeEach(() => { todos.length = 0; }) to reset state between tests, ensuring test isolation

testCoverage.summary: The test file covers only basic happy-path scenarios for addTodo and removeTodo. Critical gaps include: no validation of correct content storage/removal, no edge case handling (empty input, null, invalid indices, out-of-bounds), no test isolation (shared state between tests), and no verification that the correct items are added/removed. The tests only check array length changes, not actual data integrity. Estimated coverage: 25% - basic functionality only, missing critical error paths and edge cases.

suggestions.description: Add beforeEach hook to reset test state and prevent test interdependence. Currently tests share the same todos array, causing test pollution where one test's data affects another.
suggestions.benefits: Ensures test isolation and predictability. Each test runs with a clean slate, preventing false positives/negatives from test execution order. Makes tests more reliable and easier to debug.

suggestions.description: Replace vague assertion with specific length check. toBeGreaterThan(0) is imprecise and doesn't verify the exact behavior of adding one item.
suggestions.benefits: Provides precise verification of the addTodo function behavior. Tests both the array length AND the actual content, catching more potential bugs like duplicate insertions or incorrect values.

suggestions.description: Eliminate reliance on addTodo in removeTodo test. Tests should be independent and not depend on other functions being tested working correctly.
suggestions.benefits: Removes test coupling by directly manipulating test data instead of calling addTodo. If addTodo breaks, only its own tests fail, not removeTodo tests. Also adds verification of correct item removal.

suggestions.description: Consider using ES6 import syntax instead of CommonJS require for consistency with modern JavaScript practices.
suggestions.benefits: Aligns with modern JavaScript standards and ES modules. Provides better static analysis, tree-shaking support, and consistency with contemporary codebases. Note: requires module configuration in package.json or .mjs extension.

suggestions.description: Wrap tests in a describe block for better organization and scoping, especially as the test suite grows.
suggestions.benefits: Improves test organization and readability. Allows grouping related tests, shared setup/teardown within the suite, and clearer test output reports. Essential for maintainability as test suites grow.

suggestions.description: Add edge case and error handling tests to improve coverage and robustness.
suggestions.benefits: Ensures the code handles edge cases and invalid inputs properly. Prevents production bugs and documents expected behavior for boundary conditions. Makes the system more robust.

refactorings.summary: The test file has 6 key refactoring opportunities: (1) Add beforeEach hook for test isolation to prevent state pollution between tests, (2) Use precise assertions instead of vague checks like toBeGreaterThan(0), (3) Eliminate test coupling by directly setting up test data instead of calling functions under test, (4) Consider modernizing to ES6 imports, (5) Wrap tests in describe blocks for better organization, and (6) Add edge case tests for invalid inputs and boundary conditions. The highest impact improvements are test isolation and removing test interdependencies.

recommendations.description: Implement proper test isolation by adding beforeEach hooks to reset the todos array state between tests. Currently, tests share mutable state causing interdependence and unpredictable failures. This is the most critical issue affecting test reliability.

Add comprehensive edge case tests for invalid inputs and boundary conditions. Critical missing tests include: invalid indices for removeTodo (negative, out-of-bounds), null/empty input handling for addTodo, and verification that correct content is stored/removed (not just array length changes).

Strengthen test assertions to verify actual behavior instead of weak checks. Replace vague assertions like toBeGreaterThan(0) with precise checks that validate the exact state and content of the todos array after operations.

Remove test coupling by having each test set up its own data directly (using todos.push()) instead of calling functions under test (addTodo). This ensures that if one function breaks, it doesn't cause cascading failures in unrelated tests.
Wrap tests in describe blocks and format the code properly. The entire file is currently on single lines without proper formatting, significantly reducing readability and maintainability.
